column3: NKJV reads “Bethesda,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Bethzatha.”
NKJV includes “waiting for the moving of the water,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends with “paralyzed.”
This verse is absent from the critical text; NKJV includes it following the Textus Receptus (the angel stirring the water).
NKJV has “Take up your bed and walk,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Take up and walk.”
NKJV includes “and sought to kill Him,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
Close to the Greek; NKJV adds “also.”
Close to the Greek; “judgment” is rendered “condemnation.”
NKJV has “the will of the Father who sent Me,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the will of Him who sent Me.”
